title: Stratified advisory queue for knob recommendations and model routing
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and power users submit optimization requests (batching/caching knobs, quant profiles, routing policies) with inconsistent signal, making prioritization slow and engineering handoffs expensive. Goal: build a stratified intake and triage gateway that (1) automatically scores requests by SLO sensitivity, cost upside, and data sensitivity; (2) places them into lanes (self-serve, advisory, fast-track enterprise); and (3) produces a standardized advisory output (knob recipe + test cases + rollout plan) to reduce time-to-delivery and improve reproducibility.

Scope: intake form + autoscorer rules, lane definitions, SLAs per lane, handoff artifacts for Eng/Console/Support, observability checklist and acceptance criteria. Excluded: changes to runtime kernel code or model retraining (those become engineering follow-ups with separate epics).

Key intake fields we will require from customers: workload description, p50/p95 latency targets, current per-token cost, target cost reduction, recent token distribution (sequence length histogram), example prompts and responses, sample throughput (req/sec), current batching/cache settings, model name + pinned version, quantization constraints (allowed bit widths), security classification (public/internal/regulated), and any compliance constraints.

Autoscorer heuristics (draft): score = weighted sum of SLO sensitivity (40%), spend impact (30%), data sensitivity (15%), rollout risk (15%). Thresholds map to lanes: score < 0.3 => self-serve (auto-response + knob doc); 0.3-0.65 => advisory (PM/SE review within 5 business days); >0.65 or enterprise tag => fast-track (2-business-day SLA, dedicated concierge).

Outputs per lane: Self-serve: targeted knob checklist and knowledge base article with examples. Advisory: knob recipe, suggested quant profile candidates, routing policy template, guardrail testing matrix, and suggested A/B rollout plan. Fast-track: same as advisory + prioritized Eng ticket with reproduction steps, staging test harness, and optional dedicated runtime experiment.

Operational SLAs: auto-ack within 2h, initial lane assignment within 24h, advisory first-touch within 5 business days, fast-track first-touch within 48 business hours. Escalation triggers: regressions flagged in quality monitors post-deploy, or customer-reported production incidents => immediate escalation to on-call eng.

Success metrics: mean time from intake to recommended knobs, fraction of advisory recommendations that improve unit cost by >=15% without degrading quality beyond customer tolerance, % of requests handled in self-serve lane, and customer satisfaction (CSAT) for advisory outcomes.

Deliverables for MVP: 1) Intake form + autoscorer ruleset, 2) Lane documentation and SLAs, 3) Advisory output templates (knob recipes + rollout checklists), 4) Support/SE playbook for handoffs, 5) Dashboard tracking SLA/impact metrics.

acceptance_criteria: Intake form live in Console and linked from Support; submissions populate the advisory queue.
Autoscorer assigns lane with >=75% agreement vs. manual historical labeling (n=120).
Advisory template generates knob recipe that includes: knob values, expected trade-offs, rollout plan, and automated tests to validate (latency & quality).
SLA dashboard shows initial routing and first-touch metrics; alerts fire on missed SLAs.
Hand-off artifact for fast-track creates an Eng ticket with reproducible harness and reproduction steps attached.
rollout_steps: Week 1: Implement intake form and basic routing in staging; connect to Slack channel for notifications.
Week 2: Deploy autoscorer rules with conservative thresholds; run in shadow mode and compare to manual triage.
Week 3: Launch advisory lane (soft launch with select enterprise customers) and collect feedback; iterate templates.
Week 4: Promote to GA; monitor KPIs and tune autoscorer weights.
